newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Nov 8.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 13.7 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending November 8, and traders said volume fell on banks preparing for the increase in the reserve requirement.
Total weekly turnover fell to 33.98 million dinars ($6.8 million) from 39.36 million dinars in the previous week. Total number of transactions dropped from 195 to 172.
"Last week everybody thought about the 15 percent reserve requirement, coming into effect on November 11. Banks refrained from investments and withdrew funds instead," a trader told Reuters.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) first launched the 10 percent reserve requirement in mid-September to drain surplus liquidity from the banking sector, prevent flight from dinar funds and keep its key discount rate stable.
According to some estimates, the September measure drained between 300 and 350 million dinars from the banking system.
"It is hard to say how much money will be withdrawn from the banking system this time. And the BSE turnover fell exactly on that uncertainty," the trader said.
However, traders discounted a possibility of longer lasting negative effects of the 15 percent reserve requirement.
"We need two-three days to see the effects. In September, when the NBY opted for the measure, contraction effects on the money supply were not as significant as expected," an analyst said.
"Today we are all eyes and ears. We are waiting to see how the banks will act on the first day of the NBY measure coming into effect," another trader said.
From the early morning, traders noticed rising demand for fresh borrowing among banks. Interest rates remained nearly unchanged, ranging between 0.4 and 0.5 percent a day, traders said.
For the week ending November 8, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for nearly 75 percent of the weekly turnover with 136 deals worth 24.52 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded 32 times for a volume of 6.053 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 210 and 644 percent.

*The BSE reported two deals in the NBY short-term bonds worth 1.8 million dinars. Bonds were bought at an auction held November 6. Investor interest in the NBY bonds has been declining for the third consecutive month.
* There were two deals in wheat selling forward contracts worth 1.605 million dinars.
